BOUNDED INTEGER MULTIPLICATION: SUFFICIENT ASSEMBLY AND COST PROOF

1. Frozen scope and computation model.
Fix 1<=s,t<=256, hexadecimal digits a_i,b_j in {0,...,15}, p=65537 and N the least power of two >=s+t-1. Thus N<=512. Input words occupy addresses 1000+i and 2000+j; output words 3000..3000+N. The owned temporary region is exactly the generated fresh addresses >=10000 plus the explicitly reserved scratch set. Regions are disjoint. Arbitrary other memory, including negative signed addresses, is permitted. Initial owned words can be dirty.
The machine uses 64-bit modular words, signed comparison against zero, direct arithmetic operands and a charged halt. Word multiplication is unit cost by this explicitly chosen model; full arbitrary-size multiplication is not a primitive. The program generator uses only lengths and fixed field constants, never input digits. It creates a fixed finite program for each pair of lengths; its generation is not claimed as free work in an all-size algorithm.

2. Prime and roots.
The concrete checker tests primality by trial divisors through floor(sqrt(p)); every integer in that finite exhaustive divisor interval is checked, so a passing test is a primality certificate by the elementary least-prime-factor argument. For each actual N it sets omega=3^((p-1)/N) mod p and checks omega^N=1 and, if N>1, omega^(N/2)!=1. Since N is a power of two, these two conditions imply exact order N: every proper divisor of N divides N/2. N=1 is direct. Hence geometric-sum orthogonality and division by N are valid in F_p.

3. No wrap and unique coefficients.
Extend both digit vectors by zero to N. Ordinary product coefficients c_k=sum_{i+j=k}a_i b_j satisfy 0<=c_k<=225 min(s,t)<=57600<p. Any nonzero term has i+j<=s+t-2<N. Thus cyclic convolution has no wrap and equals the ordinary convolution, with zero tail. DFT/product/inverse computes those coefficients modulo p, by finite geometric-sum orthogonality; the least residue is exactly c_k because it is already in [0,p). The iterative positive-exponent transform has the radix-2 invariant given in ntt/NTT-APPLICATION.txt. Precomputed twiddles in the fixed program match those powers; their runtime binary literal synthesis is charged. Inverse twiddles and the final N inverse are likewise validated constants.

4. Literal modular multiply.
For x,y in [0,65536], z=xy<=2^32. The program starts with a single actual word multiplication, which is exact at W = 64. Setup constructs p,2p,...,2^15 p. Since z<p*2^16, descending greedy tests/subtractions leave z mod p: before testing 2^j p the invariant is 0<=r<2^(j+1)p; after conditionally subtracting that threshold, 0<=r<2^j p. At j=0 the result is in [0,p). A negative tentative subtraction is recognized by signed bltz; all magnitudes are below 2^33, so wrapped negative words have the intended signed meaning and no positive value crosses 2^63. Each selected quotient bit executes one extra copy. Therefore the isolated multiplication block costs33+popcount(floor(xy/p)) instructions, between 33 and49, excluding shared setup/cleanup. See ram/PROOFS.txt for the literal instructions and frame details.

5. Shared butterfly and whole transform.
Compute v=b*w mod p once. Then plus=u+v reduced once and minus=u+p-v reduced once both lie in [0,p). This yields the two required radix-2 outputs. No input is modified. A pair of fresh output cells is allocated per butterfly. Induction over the literal assembled blocks gives exactly the mathematical NTT states at every stage, for every valid input. Pointwise products and N-inverse scaling use the same proved modular multiply. Every prior non-output value remains in a known owned cell until the explicitly charged final clearing, so no missing liveness or erasure premise is assumed.

6. Carry normalization without hidden division.
The ordinary finite distributive identity gives sum_k c_k16^k = A*B. Maintain carry h<=15 min(s,t)<=3840, initially 0. Then c_k+h<=240 min(s,t)<=61440. The program obtains quotient and remainder on division by 16 via greedy subtraction of16*2^j for j=11,...,0, accumulating the selected2^j in the quotient. The same descending invariant proves 0<=remainder<16 and c_k+h=16*nextCarry+remainder; every operation is an actual allowed ISA instruction. The carry bound is preserved because floor((225m+15m)/16)=15m. Weighted telescoping proves product value is preserved. The final remaining carry is<16 because A*B<16^(s+t)<=16^(N+1); it is emitted as the final output word, allowing a leading zero. The actual program therefore emits normalized base-16 digits representing A*B, including the N=1 case.

7. Exterior/input preservation and cleanup.
Every written address is either a known output, a generated temporary or reserved scratch. Inputs never overlap these regions. Each temporary is assigned before being read, so its initial dirty value is irrelevant. After outputs have been copied, each generated temporary is set to zero by its own subtraction instruction, and all reserved scratch is similarly zeroed; setup had set the distinguished zero cell to zero. All these instructions are counted. Thus inputs and arbitrary exterior words are unchanged, all owned intermediates are zero, outputs are correct, and final accept is executed. These assertions describe the concrete program, not an assumed clean memory oracle.

8. Complete instruction bound.
Let L=log2 N and B=3NL/2 (B=0 at N=1). There are B shared butterflies, each at most58 instructions; N pointwise products and N inverse scales, each49 static instructions; 3N initial transform copies; 51N carry instructions plus one final carry copy; 35 shared setup instructions; 19 scratch clears; one accept. Let C be the number of distinct synthesized constants and H their literal instruction count. The fresh temporary count is T=7N+2B+C, each cleared in one instruction. All constants are at most65536, including carry thresholds. Thus each costs at most33 instructions; there are at most N+32 distinct constants (at most N-1 nonzero root powers, an inverse scale, zero, and 24 carry thresholds/weights). Consequently:
 static length = 60B+159N+C+H+56
              <= 60B+193N+1144.
All branches are forward and skip only optional copying, so executed steps never exceed static length. The exact literal template at N = 512 has C = 512,T = 17920 and 507701 static instructions. These space counts intentionally include retained states; they are not a claimed low-space implementation.

9. Same-ABI savings theorem.
The comparison program is generated identically except that every butterfly recomputes the same modular product immediately before its second output. Its state at each block boundary is unchanged, so every other branch, input, output and cleanup action has identical values. Its extra product costs33+popcount(floor(b*w/p)), where b and w are the actual local residues. Therefore the exact dynamic difference is the sum of those quantities over all B butterflies, always between 33B and 49B. It adds exactly 49B static instructions and no extra live cells. This proves a genuine fully charged same-output improvement over the specified recomputation control, not an improvement over a different optimized algorithm or the selected project kappa.

10. Dyadic recovery is a separate sufficient implementation route.
recovery/REPORT.txt proves E_next=(2+W)E+WM+delta, including twiddle/input error interaction; pointwise product error<=2ME+E^2+delta; inverse normalization divides the bound byN. Rational Machin/Taylor certificates establish actual twiddle bounds W=delta=2^(-b). For every admitted pair at N = 512, b = 31 suffices for coefficient error<1/2; b = 40 gives<.001. Strict closeness to a known integer recovers that integer under floor(x+1/2). Equality at a half unit is not sufficient and is a negative control. This does not provide a 64-bit cost bound for the approximate backend: its intermediates are explicitly multiword. Exact NTT and approximate FFT are two proved sufficient paths to the same product, not an unjustified mixture of field and rounded arithmetic.

11. Evidence status and first integration boundary.
The universal arguments above are informal. The portable verifier executes the concrete programs against independent schoolbook/packed-product oracles and checks every counted instruction, memory frame and clearing contract on its stated finite controls. Four local Lean lemmas, when independently audited, cover only strict integer recovery and elementary butterfly identities. They do not formally certify the assembler, all-input NTT program, prime/root procedure or floating transcendental bounds. Upstream Lean interfaces are exact pinned precedents, not rebuilt dependencies. The next project-specific step is one real consumer with a full paid-profile comparison; the present finite RAM comparison alone yields no new asymptotic kappa or selected-frontier change.
